name: BodeGalaxyContact
source:
Here we are, floating a few hundred thousand light-years outside Messier 81, or as we most fondly call it; the Bode ’ s galaxy. 
 
 “ Cameras one through six have been switched on and are collecting photos ”, Hardet pipes up over the headset. 
 
 “ Very good Hardet ”, I say completely mindlessly. It ’ s too hard to think about anything else than the fact that we are actually here. WE MADE IT. It only took three hundred years after we picked up a signal from a tiny point in M-81 to develop a functioning warp drive. I would wait it out again though, not a second thought about it. Through many trials and errors we did what we, humans, do best, and solved the problem. Almost as soon as the drive was created, the team was selected through a committee, and nations all pitched in to build the vessel; Aspiration. The sleekest thing I have ever laid eyes on. Real life science so good that it is better than any Enterprise or Star Destroyer. It is better because it is not science fiction, it is the work of our own hands. Absolutely jaw-dropping, the whole thing really is absurd. It is surreal to be part of mankind ’ s greatest accomplishment. I snap out of my daydream. 
 
 “ Alright, prepare the warp drive for a jump to our target ”, that is never going to get old to say. 
 
 “ Coordinates being processed. The drive is preparing for the jump. Prepare for a jump into warp speed. ” 
 
 Now it is time for business. The jump will bring us within a one thousand mile radius of where we located the signal. We should then be able to easily spot the planet; Mecca. At first religious fanatics fussed over the Islamic allusion. But it made the most sense to the program so we kept calling it that. We are expecting Mecca to be a planet very similar to ours, but we can not be completely right in our educated guesses. Once this warp drive comes out of the jump, we will most likely be seeing this mythical planet that may harbor the end to man ’ s eternal isolation. This ship ’ s crew will become ambassadors of a galaxy. Once that warp drive comes out of jump speed, we all become immortalized. The headset rasps to life, 
 
 “ Prepare for a rapid decrease in speed. We are coming out of warp speed ” 
 
 The stars go from ribbons to points again. We slow down to a halt. Just like we predicted, we could already see the biggest thing around. The most silent two minutes of my life passed as we looked upon our pearl. The most beautiful green and blue giant I have ever seen. Large land masses of very alien shapes and giant aquamarine oceans wrapping around the sphere. All that and three moons. A single tear drops from the corner of my eye, and a feeling of pure helplessness waves over me. This staring contest with the sphere last for another minute or so, then somebody shatters the silence, 
 
 “ Holy shit it ’ s a satellite! It ’ s a fucking satellite! They have satellites! ” 
 
 The main viewing panel lights up, and there is, in fact, a satellite. Not too different from the ones back home. We knew they were able to at least send a radio signal, but we definitely underestimated them. This is incredible, this is proof that for once and for all, we are not alone. 
 
 “ What do we do now? Do we try to send out a message? ” 
 
 “ No, let ’ s wait till they notice us. We ’ ll start moving in closer to the planet - I mean Mecca. ” 
 
 I turn on the main thrusters, and aim us toward the rock. Slowly but surely we get closer to the orbit of Mecca. As we get closer the continents and oceans become more defined. Giant mountain ranges spike off the surface, and the water turns into an even more majestic teal. The planet gradually fills up and then engulfs the windows at the front of the ship. I put the thrusters into reverse and balance us out. Gravity should keep us in orbit now. I shut off the thrusters. Now we wait. 
 
 We tried to work out what they would look like for years before we set off on our voyage. There is no way to tell and there was no point in dwelling on it much. But now we are here, on the cusp of mankind ’ s most profound moment. Any time now we should receive some kind of transmission from the planet. Considering they can not possibly be unaware of our sudden presence. We are about to make contact with an intelligent species from another galaxy. This all was science fiction two-hundred and fifty years ago, and now it is a very blunt and very surreal reality. This is all happening and no one back home has not even the slightest clue as to how our mission has been. There is no way to stay in contact with the Milky Way this far out. Here we have to wait minutes, but twelve-million light-years behind us, all the Earthlings wait patiently for our return. Assuming we return. 
 Aspiration is silent besides the typing and clicking coming from the seats of the two communications guys, Jasper and Li. Over the headset, Jasper comments, 
 
 “ Oh come on, they have to know were up here. The readings that the warp drive gives off are too unique to miss ” 
 
 “ They have also never seen them before Jasper. You ’ re going to come all this way to get impatient now? Give them some time, I would hate to intrude on their day- ”, then the most incredible thing to happened to me. The bottom right of the main viewing panel lights up with a communication message. One of the crew exclaims, 
 
 “ Holy god ” 
 
 “ Alright men. This is it. We have traveled twelve-million light-years using a warp drive we developed only years ago to the Bode ’ s galaxy, following a radio signal we picked up, and it has all led us to Mecca. We are cast in the opening scene of mankind ’ s most monumental episode. Adding to Armstrong ’ s words, we have made yet another massive leap, a warp jump, for mankind. No matter what happens it happens in the name of science and the furthering of man ’ s knowledge and reach. ” 
 The onboard system now starts beeping because it has determined the signal is for sure being directed at Aspiration. 
 
 “ Oh my god, it ’ s a file! It looks like images! ” 
 
 “ Open it up on the main panel Li ” 
 The first image vibrantly materializes instantly on the screen. A photo of four appendages in the form of an X plastered itself onto the eyes of the entire crew, reminiscent of a certain voyaging golden record. They look just like us.
retelling:
Narrator: **Hardet**, a member of the Aspiration crew, gazes through the main viewing panel with a mix of anticipation and trepidation as they hurtle towards their destination - the mysterious planet Mecca within Messier 81 (Bode's Galaxy). Three centuries have passed since the signal was first detected, and now we were finally here.

As Hardet straps in, ready to face whatever awaits them, the Aspiration's warp drive roars to life, propelling them across vast distances of space in mere moments. With a jolt that sends shockwaves throughout the ship, they find themselves only 1,000 miles away from Mecca.

Hardet watches, wide-eyed, as the planet fills the viewscreen. Despite its alien origins, it bears an uncanny resemblance to Earth - continents, oceans, and even mountain ranges stretching out before them. And then, there it was, the satellite orbiting the planet, a beacon of advanced technology.

The crew gathers around the main viewing panel, each member sharing the same sense of disbelief that this world could exist so far from home. They decide to exercise caution, waiting for any signs of life before initiating communication. The tension onboard is thick as they enter Mecca's orbit and prepare for whatever might come next.

Days turn into weeks, and finally, the crew receives a signal - a file containing images. Hardet leans forward, straining to make out what was in the image. His heart races as he sees it - beings with four appendages arranged in an X-shape, remarkably similar to humans. It's a sight that will forever change their lives and the course of human history.

For Hardet, this moment is more than just a discovery; it's validation of the endless possibilities that lie beyond our small corner of the universe. As they continue to study Mecca from orbit, they can only wonder what secrets this world holds and what awaits them on its surface. The adventure has only just begun.
